notes: Positive output matrix of the CLI-006 output-format gate: for every command path that accepts --json and/or --output, the accepted modes (text, --json, --output yaml, --output json, --quiet) are run against the pinned Go oracle. Refused modes are byte-pinned by testdata/port/cli/error-taxonomy.json and not repeated here.

Every case ran in a disposable HOME/XDG/cwd sandbox seeded from a frozen vault tree (seeds[]); the seed commands are recorded and --check refuses a generator whose commands differ from the recorded ones.
Sandbox environment: TZ=UTC, NO_COLOR=1, CI=1, SYMVAULT_PASSPHRASE with SYMVAULT_ALLOW_ENV_PASSPHRASE=1, stdin /dev/null unless a case supplies stdin.

Normalization is the numbered list 'Normalization rule N (id): ...' below (cmd/outputmodegen/main.go header, tests/output_modes.rs header and replay agree on it; a test fails when they differ); anything not listed is compared byte for byte. Every tree entry also records the permission bits (umask 022).
tree[] is the file-system diff of the sandbox root after the case, excluding the encrypted vault store (rule 11); post[] pins the resulting vault state with follow-up commands (stdout and exit only).

Some commands define a local --output flag that shadows the global one (agent profile export, agent skill export, audit export, export, template generate): there `--output yaml` names an output file; the recorded tree pins that side effect.
Normalization rule 1 (root): sandbox root and its symlink-resolved form become $ROOT (stdout, stderr, tree paths, text files, archive members, seed text files)
Normalization rule 2 (bin): the absolute path of the executed binary becomes $BIN
Normalization rule 3 (dated-id): tok-/intake-/import-YYYYMMDD-<8 hex> with a valid date becomes <prefix>-<DATE>-<RAND>
Normalization rule 4 (tmp-suffix): .age.tmp-<digits> becomes .age.tmp-<N>
Normalization rule 5 (touch-id): the boolean after 'Touch ID available: ' and in "touchIDAvailable": becomes <BOOL> (sensor property); on darwin the replay also compares the live Go and Rust values
Normalization rule 6 (gen-pw): case-declared gen-pw:N: exactly one delimited run of N alphanumerics becomes <PW> (shape verified)
Normalization rule 7 (pair-token): case-declared: the 32-character base32 pairing token becomes <TOKEN>, its first six characters <TOKEN6>
Normalization rule 8 (now-ts): case-declared: RFC 3339 timestamps within one hour of the run become <NOW>; seed timestamps stay
Normalization rule 9 (man-date): case-declared: the date field of a roff .TH header ('Mon YYYY') and the date of cobra's HISTORY line ('D-Mon-YYYY Auto generated by spf13/cobra') become <MAN-DATE>
Normalization rule 10 (opaque): case-declared tree path prefixes are recorded by presence only (device-pair invitation file, doctor token store)
Normalization rule 11 (encrypted-store): the vault's encrypted store (entries, manifest, identity, lock, search index, .git) is not in the tree diff
Normalization rule 12 (audit-fields): audit-*.log files are recorded as decoded fields (agent, action, path, field, ok, argv_hash length, signed), not bytes

Normalization rule 13 (archive-members): case-declared archive path prefixes: every file below is recorded as decompressed .tar.gz members, sorted by name (Go writes them in map order): name, type, mode, sha256 of normalized content

Normalization rule 14 (managed-fields): inside archive members the digits of a 'managed_hash: sha256:' line become <HASH> and the stamp of a 'managed_installed_at: "…"' line becomes <NOW> (install-time values)
